top.title: Parsons’ return imminent but doesn’t solve Packers’ biggest problem
top.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Micah Parsons #1 of the Green Bay Packers looks on prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers of the game at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images For all of the Green Bay Packers’ issues through ten games of the 2026 season, getting to the quarterback generally hasn’t been one of them. The Packers’ defense ranks fourth in the NFL in sacks this year, with pressure helping the team rank second in interceptions and fifth in overall passer rating against. Now the cavalry appears set to arrive. Micah Parsons is on his way back, seemingly with the intent of playing next Wednesday against the Los Angeles Rams, and his presence will only further bolster the team’s ability to get after the quarterback. It remains to be seen how he will be deployed — expect a light workload for the next few games, perhaps with him only playing on passing downs — but his return should provide an emotional lift as well as a physical one for a defense that’s already playing well. As that last phrase suggests, though, the defense isn’t really the Packers’ problem right now. That is of course the offensive line, where some recent front office decisions have helped set the table for a catastrophic season up front. One can’t help wondering if this team would be functioning better had Elgton Jenkins been kept around for one more year; had the team not invested so much money in Aaron Banks; had Anthony Belton — wait, the front office drafted him as a guard and he’s been thrust in at tackle by circumstance and the coaching staff, so that one probably isn’t on the front office. And then there is that coaching staff. From a poor overall offensive game plan last week against Minnesota to players seemingly having no idea what they’re doing on a play-to-play basis, the offensive coaches should have spent their few off days in a shortened bye week doing some serious self-evaluation. So, while Parsons’ return is an exciting storyline for the Packers, it almost feels like we’re adding the whipped cream on top of an excellent pumpkin pie while smoke is billowing out of the oven as the turkey burns. So let’s get that main course under control, yeah? top.title: ATP increases player compensation to $350m
top.description: The season-ending ATP Finals is currently taking place in Turin [Getty Images] The men's ATP Tour is promising its players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but the board has delayed a decision on hotly disputed changes to doubles until next month. The bonus pool will increase from the current $21.5m to $50m in 2028, with payments offered to players ranked in the world's top 30 at the start of each Masters 1000 event. The world number one will receive the highest bonus of $2m for each of the Masters events they play. A total of $25m will also be shared out between the world's top 250 players at the end of each season, with the goal for everyone to receive $100,000. That would make a significant difference to the finances of lower-ranked players. Players will also no longer be penalised so directly for missing tournaments through injury. World number two Jannik Sinner, for example, won five Masters events in a row between March and May, but may only qualify for 25% of his bonus as he has not been able to play since Wimbledon. Doubles changes 'a sensitive issue' Proposed changes to the doubles - which includes halving draw sizes and reducing the percentage of prize money from 20% to 10% - have received fierce opposition from the players. In October, more than 150 men's doubles players wrote an open letter to the ATP Tour urging them to reconsider "drastic" changes to the format. Chairman Andrea Gaudenzi told BBC Sport the governing body of men's tennis needed "a bit more time to reach consensus". "It is a sensitive issue," he said. "I hope we find the right balance between the players' and the tournaments' demands, and I truly hope we reach a compromise." The proposals will now be voted on next month. Doubles players have said the changes would make it "effectively impossible" for anyone outside the top 30 to make a living from the sport. There may be a hint of compromise in the air, but Gaudenzi still believes at least some of the doubles money needs to be redirected towards singles players. "It's impossible to make everyone happy. It's something we do not take lightly, but we also cannot ignore the fans and the broadcasters - [just] like any entertainment business," he said. "Whether you are a musician or an actor, it needs to be rewarded as a function of the entertainment you provide to the fans." Gaudenzi told Britain's Henry Patten, who was unhappy he and CEO Eno Polo were not present when Patten and Harri Heliovaara received the year-end number one trophy, that he had no intention of undermining their achievement. "I understand his disappointment and he's obviously also driven by what we are discussing, and I do understand it's quite emotional their side," Gaudenzi added. "But I was here in the hotel together with Eno - we were actually fighting and negotiating twelve hours a day to get this deal done - so we were really in the trenches all day long." top.title: 'I'll tell more' - Thomas Frank teases truth behind Tottenham sacking as he prepares for Crystal Palace rescue mission
top.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Newcastle United - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Thomas Frank has officially been unveiled as the new Crystal Palace manager, and the Dane wasted no time in addressing his complicated history with former employers Tottenham. As he prepares to lead the struggling Eagles out of the Premier League relegation zone, Frank suggested there is a deeper story behind his short-lived tenure in North London. Frank takes Palace reins after turbulent Spurs spell Crystal Palace appointed the 53-year-old Dane on Monday on a contract until June 2029, replacing Pierre Sage. Thursday afternoon's unveiling marked Frank's first managerial role since Tottenham sacked him earlier this year after under eight months in charge. Before his troubled north London stint, Frank established Brentford in the Premier League and earned a Manager of the Year nomination. Following his Spurs dismissal, he travelled across Japan, Australia, and Denmark before taking over the Eagles. Dane promises future clarity on Tottenham departure Expecting questions about his former club, Frank admitted: "I know today is a lot about me". While keeping the focus on Palace, he suggested the full story of his Spurs exit will eventually surface. "It’s something I’ve… maybe one day I’ll tell a little bit more about it," Frank said. "I understand why it’s also interesting. I think it’s more about Palace in general today. What can I say? I always said the day I got sacked, I’ll have time to travel, so I think I was relatively quick over it." He added: "But of course you want success, and I’m competitive, so I think that answer probably demands a little bit more time, which I am happy to do one day." Infamous Arsenal cup gaffe still baffles new Eagles boss Frank's Spurs spell unravelled in January when he was pictured drinking from an Arsenal coffee cup ahead of a 3-2 defeat to Bournemouth. For fans already disillusioned with his style of play, the blunder was the final straw, and a five-match winless league run sealed his sacking a month later. Asked if he might accidentally use a cup belonging to Palace's fierce rivals Brighton, Frank smiled. "I hope not," he replied, adding: "I still think it’s a fantastic story." He remains baffled by the backlash to the honest mistake: "I know, and I still don’t understand, how anyone can think that I will drink from a cup from an opponent’s team, that their supporters don’t like, on purpose. Come on. But what a story, huh, to discuss?" Relegation battle and Europa League test await Frank faces an immediate test in lifting Crystal Palace off the bottom of the Premier League table, starting with Saturday's trip to Coventry. Arresting their domestic slump quickly is vital to sparking a survival push. He must also balance European duties, with Palace hosting Real Sociedad in the Europa League next Thursday. Managing energy levels across both fronts will be crucial as the Dane bids to restore his Premier League credentials.

top.title: Sophie Cunningham challenges her male haters to 3-point contest
top.description: Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images WNBA star Sophie Cunningham has had enough of armchair critics, and she’s ready to settle things on the court. Sophie Cunningham’s challenge goes straight at one of the tiredest takes in basketball, the idea that any decent guy from the local rec league could hold his own against a WNBA pro. Even with women’s basketball bigger than ever, female players still get hit with the same skepticism about their game every time they log online. The funny thing is, whenever someone actually steps onto the court to test it, reality hits fast. Fans saw Sparks guard Rae Burrell cruise past streamer N3on in a one-on-one, a quick reminder that pro-level talent is on a completely different planet than couch-cushion confidence. Sophie Cunningham challenges men to a three-point contest Speaking on her podcast , Sophie Cunningham finally had enough of guys talking trash about women’s sports from the couch, and decided to call their bluff. She said: “Dude, I think I’ve said enough about where my stance is on this when it comes to boys and girls, I’ll say. But when it comes to regular Joes—what kills me, and even the guys know this—the people talking bad on us women professional athletes, it doesn’t matter the sport, it’s all these men who are laying on the couch, probably eating potato chips. It used to drive me crazy, but now I’m just like, I feel bad for you guys because I don’t know—why are you guys coming after us? “So, what I’m going to say is I think I want to do a challenge here to our listeners, or if you don’t listen, maybe this clip will get out there. I want to find some average Joes—like in the YMCA league and the rec league—who think that they can outshoot me, and have a three-point competition because I’m going to smack that a** every single day of the week. So, I’m challenging all these little people behind the screen who think they can beat me. You won’t.” Honestly, it would be must-see TV. Watching a guy from the local rec league try to keep up with a WNBA player would settle the debate and provide great entertainment, especially considering Cunningham actually shot a higher three-point percentage than Steph Curry this past season. Good luck to whoever volunteers. top.title: Taraba varsity ASUU conditionally suspends strike
top.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University (TSU) Branch, has announced the conditional suspension of its ongoing industrial action with immediate effect. In a statement issued on Friday and signed by the Branch Chairman, Dr. Joshua Garba Mbave, the union disclosed that its Congress resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive, and indefinite strike which commenced on October 12, 2026 following an emergency meeting at the ASUU-TSU Secretariat in Jalingo. While confirming the return to academic activities effective November 20, 2026, the union cautioned that sustaining industrial harmony and an uninterrupted academic calendar hinges on mutual trust, accountability, and strict adherence to agreed commitments. ASUU-TSU urged the Taraba State Government, the University Management, and all relevant stakeholders to demonstrate good faith by ensuring the timely and full implementation of all resolutions contained in the joint communiqué and the Memorandum of Action (MoA) to avert a recurrence of the dispute. The union expressed profound appreciation to Governor Agbu Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service, and the University Management for their constructive engagement and intervention toward resolving the standoff. It also thanked students, parents, staff, and the wider university community for their patience, solidarity, and understanding throughout the five-week industrial action, appealing for continued cooperation as normal academic activities resume. top.title: Blues fan snubs Homes Under the Hammer over Villa's Dion Dublin
top.description: Birmingham City supporter George Pollock, pictured with his wife Catherine, turned down the chance of being on the show [George Pollock] A Birmingham City fan has revealed why he refused to appear on Homes Under the Hammer after discovering the presenter was former Aston Villa striker Dion Dublin. George Pollock and his wife Catherine, from Castle Bromwich, were approached by the BBC daytime show's production team after buying a property at auction to renovate and sell on. While Catherine jumped at the chance to feature on the programme, George was rather less enthusiastic, and finding out who would be presenting the episode did not help. George said: "Catherine turned around and told me, 'It's going to be Dion Dublin.' I was like, 'Oh, you do it!' "I didn't really want to spend a day with a Villa player." Dublin played for Aston Villa between 1998 and 2002, scoring 48 goals in 65 appearances, becoming a popular figure at Villa Park. Catherine, meanwhile, was happy to go ahead with the filming, but she knew her husband would not feel the same after learning who would be presenting their episode. "If he says he doesn't want to do something, he's probably not going to. Especially when it comes to football," joked Catherine, who appeared in the episode alone. When the reason for her husband's absence was revealed on the show, Dublin could not help but laugh and commend the fan. "I love that he's a proper Blues fan, good lad," he said. Dion Dublin played for Aston Villa between 1998 and 2002 [BBC/lion production] The couple had bought the property with plans to do it up before selling it but had not initially expected their renovation project to end up on television. The Homes Under the Hammer team regularly keep an eye on property auctions to find potential homes and buyers to feature on the show. For lifelong Blues supporter George, however, there was one problem with the whole arrangement. He explained that his love of Birmingham City was passed down by his father, making the prospect of spending a day with a former Villa player a step too far. He joked: "When you're raised on it, you can't get rid of it and I'm sure the other side would have done the exact same. "I've heard he was a good sport about it," added George, who never did meet Dublin. The story has since sparked plenty of amusement on social media, with football fans enjoying the light-hearted rivalry. George said: "It's petty but it's fun petty." top.title: Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session filmed by drone and uploaded online amidst security breach
top.description: Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session filmed by drone and uploaded online amidst security breach originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mauricio Pochettino's very first day on the job at Manchester United has already been met with a crisis as the club was victim of an embarrassing security breach. The Argentine has only just arrived as new United manager, flying into Manchester on Wednesday morning, having departed straight after his final game with the U.S. national team on Tuesday night. He has only a few days to prepare for his debut as Red Devils' boss, a difficult challenge on the road at Anfield. Now, it seems that much of the work he did in his first training session might have to be scrapped as his session was leaked publicly and available to the rest of the world. MORE: All the latest Man United news | Who is on Pochettino's Man United backroom staff? Individual films Man United training session with drone An unknown individual managed to film 12 minutes of Pochettino's first training session at the club's Carrington training ground, which is closed to media and the public. The individual flew a drone high above the training ground and filmed Pochettino running drills and giving tactical instructions to his new Red Devils squad, an event which is usually highly confidential and secretive as to avoid giving opponents clear insight into how teams will line up or approach matches. The video, uploaded to YouTube with the pilot of the drone also narrating the footage, shows various selections of players broken off into position groups training on their own before coming together to take tactical instructions from Pochettino. It appears that the pilot uses a drone with impressive zoom capabilities, and does not seem to cross over the Carrington training ground itself to capture the footage. top.title: Urban Meyer Shoots Down Desmond Howard’s Heisman Thoughts
top.description: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates after scoring a touchdown in the second half of the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium on Nov. 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. Former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer has publicly rejected 1991 Heisman winner Desmond Howard’s doubts about Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith’s candidacy for the trophy. Howard, speaking on ESPN’s First Take on Nov. 13, questioned whether Smith has delivered in marquee games. “In the last two years, give me one game where Jeremiah Smith … was the difference in a big game,” Howard said. “As much as he puts up these magnificent numbers and these one-handed catches, I need moments against the top competition that make me say ‘he was the guy.'” Meyer, appearing on The Triple Option podcast, was direct in response . “He’s gonna win [the Heisman]. Are we kidding?” he said. Acknowledging that Ohio State’s losses to USC (30-18) and Oregon (41-28) left a “bad taste,” Meyer defended the junior receiver’s effort: “Did he do everything possible to go win those games? The fact that Desmond Howard said, ‘I don’t see him making plays in the big games’… I don’t agree with that.” Smith caught 10 passes for 83 yards and a touchdown at USC and seven for 133 yards and a score against Oregon. Meyer added that the award will partly reflect Smith’s body of work, including a national title as a freshman, while insisting the trophy still goes to the best player. After getting blocked by Aday Mara, the Thunder’s 7ft 3in offseason pickup clearly designed to counter the even more towering Wembanyama, he leaned over his knees and muttered furiously to himself as if trying to exorcise an intrusive thought. top.title: Tonda Eckert signs Southampton contract extension after ‘Spygate’ scandal
top.description: Tonda Eckert has signed a contract extension at Southampton after surviving the storm of the ‘Spygate’ scandal . Eckert found himself under immense scrutiny after Southampton were caught spying on their Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough last season. An investigation found Saints had also spied on two other teams that seasons and the club were subsequently kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points at the start of the season season, admitting to three breaches of EFL regulations. Eckert accepted responsibility as Southampton opted to stand by their manager despite the controversy, and he was later given a six-week suspended ban - keeping him on the touchline barring any further offences. And despite the hindrance of a points deduction, Southampton have started the season in fine form under Eckert, with the club five points off top spot. The German has now been rewarded with a contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2029. Eckert said: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now. "There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come." Saints are unbeaten in their last 17 home matches, with Eckert only experiencing one defeat at St Mary’s during his tenure. The matchup marks the PWHL’s return to Pittsburgh, where PPG Paints Arena previously hosted a neutral-site game during the league’s inaugural season. nigeria.title: Court Rejects Atiku’s Bid To Tender Fresh Evidence In Suit Seeking Tinubu’s Disqualification
nigeria.description: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice President and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to present fresh evidence in his suit seeking to prevent President Bola Tinubu from contesting the 2027 presidential election over allegations of forgery of his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate. The judge held that the time allowed by law to present evidence in a pre-election suit was 14 days, in line with Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution. Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and the other defendants that allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence would alter the nature of the original case and violate the provisions of the Constitution. In his ruling on Atiku’s application to amend the originating summons in the suit against Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the judge held that the former vice president attempted to mislead the court by claiming that the proposed amendment would not introduce fresh issues. Justice Ekwo said that, after carefully examining the application, the court found that the ADC presidential candidate sought to substitute existing evidence with new evidence which, if allowed, would circumvent Section 285(9) of the Constitution, which requires such evidence to be presented within 14 days. A man walks past the Federal High Court premises in Abuja, on April 22, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) According to the judge, allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence through the back door would amount to a fundamental injustice against the defendants. Meanwhile, following an agreement among the lawyers, the judge fixed December 2 for the hearing of the substantive suit. Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendments to his case challenging Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election. In the main suit, Atiku and the ADC asked Justice Ekwo to disqualify Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election. They challenged the authenticity of Tinubu’s NYSC discharge certificate submitted to INEC by the APC. nigeria.description: Former Rivers State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Tonye Cole, has denied that his decision to support the party’s political arrangement ahead of the 2027 elections was motivated by a promise of a future governorship ticket. Cole said his priority was to change the perception of Rivers State as a place associated with violence and political strongmen, arguing that peace and security were essential to attracting investment to the state. He spoke on Friday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief , where he was asked whether he had been promised an opportunity to pursue his governorship ambition in the future. “No, and that is not what is driving me,” he replied. “What is driving me is that if you cannot bring peace and security and change the narrative of Rivers State, investment will not come to Rivers State. So the first aspect of it is that we must change the mindset of everyone that when they talk about Rivers State, violence, strongman, no gentlemen, loud, all of that tagline must change. “If I cannot be the face of what the future of Rivers State politics should look like, then we have a problem,” he added. ﻿ Cole, who emerged as the APC governorship candidate in 2019 and 2023, withdrew from the party’s 2027 governorship race in May following consultations and efforts to reconcile rival factions within the state chapter. He subsequently aligned with the Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political arrangement led by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, which is backing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Explaining his decision to remain with the APC group that predated the current political arrangement, Cole said he wanted to ensure that members who had worked to build the party were not sidelined. “For me, abandoning those who were in APC who worked was not the question. So I decided that I was going to stay with them so that they would have a voice. He added that the decision to bring different political interests together was informed by the need to prevent divisions that had previously weakened the APC in Rivers State. ‘No Differences With Wike’ A combo of Cole, Wike, and logos of the APC and PDP Wike holds near-total control over the formal political institutions and party structures in Rivers State. nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has slammed Dr. Adetokunbo Pearse over his recent series of interviews allegedly maligning and disparaging President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. nigeria.title: Uche Nnaji: HURIWA accuses ICPC of political persecution, demands halt to prosecution
nigeria.description: … Alleges plot to weaken Mbah’s political challenger … Warns against weaponising anti-graft agencies ahead of 2027 elections By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) on Friday accused the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) of using its prosecution of former Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, Uche Nnaji, to advance political interests in Enugu State, demanding an immediate halt to the case pending an independent review. The rights group alleged that the continued prosecution of Nnaji, amid the controversy surrounding his academic qualifications, raises serious questions about the neutrality and independence of the anti-corruption agency, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a press statement signed by its National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, HURIWA warned that criminal prosecution must not become an instrument for intimidating opposition figures, weakening political challengers or protecting incumbent office holders. The association alleged that Nnaji’s prosecution increasingly bears the appearance of a political project designed to undermine one of the formidable challengers to Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah. It claimed that the former minister remains one of the few politicians capable of mounting a serious challenge to Mbah’s political dominance, raising concerns that state institutions could be deployed to influence the state’s political landscape. HURIWA said: “The ICPC must stop this prosecution if it cannot convincingly establish that the process is independent, evidence-driven and free from political considerations. Nigerians must not allow persecution to disguise itself as prosecution.” The group maintained that while allegations against Nnaji should be subjected to lawful investigation and accountability, they must not provide a justification for selective deployment of state institutions against political actors. It also recalled that Nnaji had approached the Federal High Court to compel the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, to release his academic transcript, noting that the controversy surrounding his academic records remained contentious. According to HURIWA, the circumstances surrounding the investigation and prosecution require closer scrutiny to ensure that the anti-corruption agency is not acting on political considerations. The association further accused the Federal Government of failing to prevent anti-corruption institutions from operating in ways that could intimidate perceived political opponents and distort the country’s multiparty democratic process. nigeria.title: 2030: FG takes decisive action to end open defecation with Executive Order
nigeria.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – IN a renewed commitment, the Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s drive towards ending open defecation by 2030. The unveiling of the Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025 coincided with the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja on Thursday. Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes. Shettima said the order marks a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress. He called on state and local governments to strengthen accountability, increase sanitation financing and sustain community-led behavioural change He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas have attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remain the only states certified as ODF nationwide. While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President warned that the country still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available. He also cautioned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements. According to him, Nigeria must prioritise sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change to achieve the 2030 target. He also called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions, while urging development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support. Shettima, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, noting that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda. Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality,” the Vice President highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls. He noted that inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermines their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. nigeria.description: The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration. Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Political Matters in the Office of the Vice President, said the president’s associates could be giving him a false impression of his popularity by relying on assurances from governors and party loyalists rather than listening to ordinary Nigerians. He made the remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief programme. The PRP chairman said his assessment of public sentiment was based on his grassroots political connections and familiarity with the administration, which he initially supported. “I’m a politician. I lead a political party that is entirely grassroots-based. I have very strong organic links with the people. I followed the Tinubu administration from inception. Initially, I was even part of it,” he said. ﻿ Baba-Ahmed said he was familiar with the feelings of Nigerians and was not exaggerating the widespread dissatisfaction with the government. He identified poverty, economic mismanagement, corruption and insecurity as some of the issues contributing to the growing distance between the administration and the people. He also suggested that some political associates were giving Tinubu assurances about his chances of securing re-election in 2027 without adequately reflecting the mood of Nigerians. “There are a lot of people who are telling President Tinubu lies if he thinks himself, and they think that the people are with them. Just look at wherever APC goes. People either chase them away or they trigger violence,” he said. ‘Bamayi’ Baba-Ahmed also described the ‘Bamayi’ chants directed at the president as an expression of widespread dissatisfaction, insisting that the sentiment was not restricted to young people or northern Nigerians. “This Bamayi thing, it’s not just a slogan that young people throw at APC. It’s genuinely an organic element of the way Nigerians, not just northerners, Nigerians feel,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. Between beach days, the bustling Central Market in Port Louis, the lush trails of Black River Gorges National Park, and Casela Nature Parks keep a week-long itinerary full without ever feeling hectic. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. entertainment.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. This philosophy also came through in her cover interview with THISDAY Glitterati ahead of the summit, where she offered a compelling perspective on the distinction between holding a powerful position and exercising genuine influence. “A powerful position gives you formal authority. Influence determines how deeply your leadership shapes people’s thinking, decisions and actions. A title may secure your place in a meeting, but credibility makes people listen,” she explained. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? What result did you produce? What changed because of your leadership?” she asked, highlighting the importance of making professional value visible to the decision-makers who influence career progression and boardroom opportunities. “There is no need to diminish your achievements to make others comfortable. entertainment.description: The Metropolitan Club, Lagos, was transformed into a gathering of some of the most influential names in Nigeria’s energy industry as the Women in Energy Network (WIEN) hosted its 2026 Gala & Awards. Bringing together industry leaders, policymakers, corporate executives and other distinguished guests, the evening marked six years of WIEN’s advocacy for greater representation, inclusion and leadership opportunities for women across the energy value chain. Beyond the glamour, elegant conversations and celebrations, the event carried a clear message: it is time to move beyond conversations about inclusion and focus on measurable progress. The Honourable Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajia Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim , delivered the special address, ably represented by Dr Adedayo Benjamins-Laniyi , Director-General/Chief Executive Officer of the Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women Development . In her address, WIEN President Eyono Fatayi-Williams emphasised that progress must be visible, measurable and sustained. “As we celebrate six years, we also have to ask ourselves an important question: What do the next six years look like? Because we cannot spend the next six years having the same conversations we have had in the last six years. We cannot continue to talk about inclusion without asking what has changed,” Fatayi-Williams challenged the industry. The evening also featured a keynote address by Dr Mutiu Sunmonu (CON) , Chairman of The Sage Centre for Leadership Excellence, who shared perspectives on leadership and the importance of creating opportunities for women to contribute meaningfully to the sector. Six Years of Building Opportunities for Women Reflecting on the organisation’s growth and the realities of navigating the energy sector, WIEN Board of Trustees Chairperson, Dr Cecilia Aqua Umoren , challenged guests to strive for true parity. “In the six years that WIEN has been in existence, we have created more opportunities for women, resulting in numerous appointments and an expanded STEM pipeline. However, progress is not parity; we are ultimately aiming for true parity. We must acknowledge that most leadership positions today are occupied by men, meaning we cannot achieve our objectives without partnering with them to create access. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. sports.title: ATP increases player compensation to $350m
sports.description: The season-ending ATP Finals is currently taking place in Turin [Getty Images] The men's ATP Tour is promising its players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but the board has delayed a decision on hotly disputed changes to doubles until next month. The bonus pool will increase from the current $21.5m to $50m in 2028, with payments offered to players ranked in the world's top 30 at the start of each Masters 1000 event. The world number one will receive the highest bonus of $2m for each of the Masters events they play. A total of $25m will also be shared out between the world's top 250 players at the end of each season, with the goal for everyone to receive $100,000. That would make a significant difference to the finances of lower-ranked players. Players will also no longer be penalised so directly for missing tournaments through injury. World number two Jannik Sinner, for example, won five Masters events in a row between March and May, but may only qualify for 25% of his bonus as he has not been able to play since Wimbledon. Doubles changes 'a sensitive issue' Proposed changes to the doubles - which includes halving draw sizes and reducing the percentage of prize money from 20% to 10% - have received fierce opposition from the players. In October, more than 150 men's doubles players wrote an open letter to the ATP Tour urging them to reconsider "drastic" changes to the format. Chairman Andrea Gaudenzi told BBC Sport the governing body of men's tennis needed "a bit more time to reach consensus". "It is a sensitive issue," he said. "I hope we find the right balance between the players' and the tournaments' demands, and I truly hope we reach a compromise." The proposals will now be voted on next month. Doubles players have said the changes would make it "effectively impossible" for anyone outside the top 30 to make a living from the sport. There may be a hint of compromise in the air, but Gaudenzi still believes at least some of the doubles money needs to be redirected towards singles players. "It's impossible to make everyone happy. It's something we do not take lightly, but we also cannot ignore the fans and the broadcasters - [just] like any entertainment business," he said. "Whether you are a musician or an actor, it needs to be rewarded as a function of the entertainment you provide to the fans." Gaudenzi told Britain's Henry Patten, who was unhappy he and CEO Eno Polo were not present when Patten and Harri Heliovaara received the year-end number one trophy, that he had no intention of undermining their achievement. "I understand his disappointment and he's obviously also driven by what we are discussing, and I do understand it's quite emotional their side," Gaudenzi added. "But I was here in the hotel together with Eno - we were actually fighting and negotiating twelve hours a day to get this deal done - so we were really in the trenches all day long." sports.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Newcastle United - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Thomas Frank has officially been unveiled as the new Crystal Palace manager, and the Dane wasted no time in addressing his complicated history with former employers Tottenham. As he prepares to lead the struggling Eagles out of the Premier League relegation zone, Frank suggested there is a deeper story behind his short-lived tenure in North London. Frank takes Palace reins after turbulent Spurs spell Crystal Palace appointed the 53-year-old Dane on Monday on a contract until June 2029, replacing Pierre Sage. Thursday afternoon's unveiling marked Frank's first managerial role since Tottenham sacked him earlier this year after under eight months in charge. Before his troubled north London stint, Frank established Brentford in the Premier League and earned a Manager of the Year nomination. Following his Spurs dismissal, he travelled across Japan, Australia, and Denmark before taking over the Eagles. Dane promises future clarity on Tottenham departure Expecting questions about his former club, Frank admitted: "I know today is a lot about me". While keeping the focus on Palace, he suggested the full story of his Spurs exit will eventually surface. "It’s something I’ve… maybe one day I’ll tell a little bit more about it," Frank said. "I understand why it’s also interesting. I think it’s more about Palace in general today. What can I say? I always said the day I got sacked, I’ll have time to travel, so I think I was relatively quick over it." He added: "But of course you want success, and I’m competitive, so I think that answer probably demands a little bit more time, which I am happy to do one day." Infamous Arsenal cup gaffe still baffles new Eagles boss Frank's Spurs spell unravelled in January when he was pictured drinking from an Arsenal coffee cup ahead of a 3-2 defeat to Bournemouth. For fans already disillusioned with his style of play, the blunder was the final straw, and a five-match winless league run sealed his sacking a month later. Asked if he might accidentally use a cup belonging to Palace's fierce rivals Brighton, Frank smiled. "I hope not," he replied, adding: "I still think it’s a fantastic story." He remains baffled by the backlash to the honest mistake: "I know, and I still don’t understand, how anyone can think that I will drink from a cup from an opponent’s team, that their supporters don’t like, on purpose. Come on. But what a story, huh, to discuss?" sports.title: Sophie Cunningham challenges her male haters to 3-point contest
sports.description: Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images WNBA star Sophie Cunningham has had enough of armchair critics, and she’s ready to settle things on the court. Sophie Cunningham’s challenge goes straight at one of the tiredest takes in basketball, the idea that any decent guy from the local rec league could hold his own against a WNBA pro. Even with women’s basketball bigger than ever, female players still get hit with the same skepticism about their game every time they log online. The funny thing is, whenever someone actually steps onto the court to test it, reality hits fast. Fans saw Sparks guard Rae Burrell cruise past streamer N3on in a one-on-one, a quick reminder that pro-level talent is on a completely different planet than couch-cushion confidence. Sophie Cunningham challenges men to a three-point contest Speaking on her podcast , Sophie Cunningham finally had enough of guys talking trash about women’s sports from the couch, and decided to call their bluff. She said: “Dude, I think I’ve said enough about where my stance is on this when it comes to boys and girls, I’ll say. But when it comes to regular Joes—what kills me, and even the guys know this—the people talking bad on us women professional athletes, it doesn’t matter the sport, it’s all these men who are laying on the couch, probably eating potato chips. It used to drive me crazy, but now I’m just like, I feel bad for you guys because I don’t know—why are you guys coming after us? “So, what I’m going to say is I think I want to do a challenge here to our listeners, or if you don’t listen, maybe this clip will get out there. I want to find some average Joes—like in the YMCA league and the rec league—who think that they can outshoot me, and have a three-point competition because I’m going to smack that a** every single day of the week. So, I’m challenging all these little people behind the screen who think they can beat me. You won’t.” Honestly, it would be must-see TV. Watching a guy from the local rec league try to keep up with a WNBA player would settle the debate and provide great entertainment, especially considering Cunningham actually shot a higher three-point percentage than Steph Curry this past season. Good luck to whoever volunteers. sports.description: Birmingham City supporter George Pollock, pictured with his wife Catherine, turned down the chance of being on the show [George Pollock] A Birmingham City fan has revealed why he refused to appear on Homes Under the Hammer after discovering the presenter was former Aston Villa striker Dion Dublin. George Pollock and his wife Catherine, from Castle Bromwich, were approached by the BBC daytime show's production team after buying a property at auction to renovate and sell on. While Catherine jumped at the chance to feature on the programme, George was rather less enthusiastic, and finding out who would be presenting the episode did not help. George said: "Catherine turned around and told me, 'It's going to be Dion Dublin.' I was like, 'Oh, you do it!' "I didn't really want to spend a day with a Villa player." Dublin played for Aston Villa between 1998 and 2002, scoring 48 goals in 65 appearances, becoming a popular figure at Villa Park. Catherine, meanwhile, was happy to go ahead with the filming, but she knew her husband would not feel the same after learning who would be presenting their episode. "If he says he doesn't want to do something, he's probably not going to. Especially when it comes to football," joked Catherine, who appeared in the episode alone. When the reason for her husband's absence was revealed on the show, Dublin could not help but laugh and commend the fan. "I love that he's a proper Blues fan, good lad," he said. Dion Dublin played for Aston Villa between 1998 and 2002 [BBC/lion production] The couple had bought the property with plans to do it up before selling it but had not initially expected their renovation project to end up on television. The Homes Under the Hammer team regularly keep an eye on property auctions to find potential homes and buyers to feature on the show. For lifelong Blues supporter George, however, there was one problem with the whole arrangement. He explained that his love of Birmingham City was passed down by his father, making the prospect of spending a day with a former Villa player a step too far. He joked: "When you're raised on it, you can't get rid of it and I'm sure the other side would have done the exact same. "I've heard he was a good sport about it," added George, who never did meet Dublin. The story has since sparked plenty of amusement on social media, with football fans enjoying the light-hearted rivalry. George said: "It's petty but it's fun petty." Howard, speaking on ESPN’s First Take on Nov. 13, questioned whether Smith has delivered in marquee games. “In the last two years, give me one game where Jeremiah Smith … was the difference in a big game,” Howard said. “As much as he puts up these magnificent numbers and these one-handed catches, I need moments against the top competition that make me say ‘he was the guy.'” Meyer, appearing on The Triple Option podcast, was direct in response . “He’s gonna win [the Heisman]. Are we kidding?” he said. Acknowledging that Ohio State’s losses to USC (30-18) and Oregon (41-28) left a “bad taste,” Meyer defended the junior receiver’s effort: “Did he do everything possible to go win those games? Yeah, he did. The fact that Desmond Howard said, ‘I don’t see him making plays in the big games’… I don’t agree with that.” Smith caught 10 passes for 83 yards and a touchdown at USC and seven for 133 yards and a score against Oregon. Meyer added that the award will partly reflect Smith’s body of work, including a national title as a freshman, while insisting the trophy still goes to the best player. sports.title: Tonda Eckert signs Southampton contract extension after ‘Spygate’ scandal
sports.description: Tonda Eckert has signed a contract extension at Southampton after surviving the storm of the ‘Spygate’ scandal . Eckert found himself under immense scrutiny after Southampton were caught spying on their Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough last season. An investigation found Saints had also spied on two other teams that seasons and the club were subsequently kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points at the start of the season season, admitting to three breaches of EFL regulations. Eckert accepted responsibility as Southampton opted to stand by their manager despite the controversy, and he was later given a six-week suspended ban - keeping him on the touchline barring any further offences. And despite the hindrance of a points deduction, Southampton have started the season in fine form under Eckert, with the club five points off top spot. The German has now been rewarded with a contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2029. Eckert said: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now. "There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come." Saints are unbeaten in their last 17 home matches, with Eckert only experiencing one defeat at St Mary’s during his tenure. "I think it's a great commitment from both sides; from the club to Tonda, and from Tonda to the club. I'm very happy that we have achieved this agreement before the end of the international window, allowing us to go into the busy schedule that is ahead of us with clarity,” sporting director Johannes Spors said. sports.title: Wild GM Responds to Dylan Larkin Trade Package Rumors
sports.description: The Dylan Larkin trade saga has produced plenty of rumors, but Minnesota Wild general manager Bill Guerin wants to make one thing clear: Nobody outside the two organizations knows exactly what Minnesota has offered the Detroit Red Wings. With reports circulating about a massive package involving several players and multiple first-round draft picks, Guerin recently pushed back on the speculation. His comments raise an interesting question about how much of the reported trade package is actually accurate.’ Mar 21, 2026; Saint Paul, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Wild general manager Bill Guerin presents defensemen Jared Spurgeon (46) with a silver stick in honor of his 1000 career NHL games before a tilt against the Dallas Stars at Grand Casino Arena. Mandatory Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bill Guerin Addresses Dylan Larkin Trade Rumors During a November 12 appearance on Minneapolis radio, Guerin was asked about reports that Minnesota had included young forward Danila Yurov in a potential deal for Larkin. Rather than confirming or denying the rumored offer, the Wild GM made it clear that the public doesn’t know what has been discussed. “Look, I know there are reports out there that we have offered him up, but nobody knows what I’ve offered, except Detroit,” Guerin said, according to NHL.com . Guerin’s response is significant because several reports have detailed potential Minnesota trade packages as the Wild continue pursuing Larkin. As Heavy reported , the Minnesota GM’s comments cast doubt on the accuracy of the rumored offers without eliminating the possibility that Yurov has been discussed. What Have the Wild Reportedly Offered Detroit? One of the most substantial reported packages included Yurov, former Michigan State standout Charlie Stramel, veteran forward Ryan Hartman, and two first-round draft picks. The Red Wings reportedly turned down that offer , although the exact details have not been publicly confirmed by either organization. Other reports have suggested different combinations of prospects and draft selections, including a potential package centered around Yurov and three first-round picks. That creates considerable uncertainty about what Minnesota has actually put on the table and whether Detroit has received an offer it would seriously consider accepting. For the Red Wings, the situation remains complicated because Larkin’s value goes beyond his offensive production. Detroit would need a significant return for its longtime center, particularly with interim general manager Shawn Horcoff attempting to improve the organization’s long-term outlook. Does Guerin’s Response Change Anything? The most important distinction is that Guerin did not publicly deny making an offer for Larkin. He also didn’t explicitly rule out including Yurov, meaning his comments should not be interpreted as proof that the reported trade packages are entirely false. sports.title: Travis Kelce Gets Caitlin Clark To Reveal Her Notre Dame Loyalty On New Heights
sports.description: Caitlin Clark Caitlin Clark has a hard time slipping through any building unnoticed. So a hat and a pair of sunglasses had to do the heavy lifting at Notre Dame Stadium. The Indiana Fever star revealed this week on the ‘New Heights’ podcast that she attended Notre Dame’s win over then-No. 1 Miami on Nov. 7 in a low-key disguise. She also admitted that she grew up a Fighting Irish fan and nearly picked the program for college. Travis Kelce wanted to know why an Iowa icon was watching Notre Dame. Clark explained that it has become a yearly habit. “ I try to make it to, like, one Notre Dame game a year. I grew up a Notre Dame fan. I wanted to go to Notre Dame ,” Clark said. “I try to make it to one Notre Dame game a year. I grew up a Notre Dame fan.” — Caitlin Clark on attending Notre Dame’s win over No. 1 Miami — Drew Mentock (@AndrewMentock) November 19, 2026 The setup was part of the fun. Clark did not ask for a field pass. She took ordinary seats, and her description is hard to beat. “ I had on like a hat and sunglasses, and I was actually in the second to last row of like the normal bowl, like normal seats ,” Clark said. “ Yeah, nobody knew, I mean some people knew. ” For Clark, the draw was the atmosphere, including a tailgate beforehand with actor Jason Sudeikis, who was the guest picker on College GameDay that week. She picked a good night for it. Notre Dame beat Miami 31-24 in a game that ended with a controversial late call. The win knocked the Hurricanes off the top spot, and quarterback CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and 3 touchdowns. The Irish are now 9-1. Marcus Freeman’s team is poised to return to the College Football Playoff, so Clark picked a season-defining night to show up. Notre Dame faces SMU next, and the Irish will try to keep that momentum going. Why Caitlin Clark Still Has Notre Dame In Her Heart The loyalty goes back to her recruiting days in 2019. Clark narrowed her list to Iowa, Iowa State, and Notre Dame. Her family leaned toward South Bend, and she has never hidden that. “ They recruited me. It was between Notre Dame and Iowa, and then I picked Iowa ,” Clark said. “ But Notre Dame is just so cool, the history of everything. ” She has been even more direct before. “ My family wanted me to go to Notre Dame ,” Clark has said. “ But it’s NOTRE DAME! ‘Rudy’ was one of my favorite movies. How could you not pick Notre Dame? ” There is one limit to her loyalty, and Hawkeyes fans will like it. Clark would not cheer for the Irish if they ever faced Iowa. The two schools met 24 times between 1921 and 1968, but the series went quiet decades ago. A conversation with then-Iowa assistant coach Jan Jensen helped tip her final call toward the Hawkeyes. She went on to become the face of Iowa basketball, but her Notre Dame fandom never went away. Her fall has been busy outside the WNBA season. sports.title: Cadillac Will Stay a Ferrari Customer Through 2029 and Wait for F1’s V8 Engines
sports.description: Cadillac will stay a Ferrari customer through 2029 and debut its own power unit in 2030, when F1 plans to switch to V8s, CEO Dan Towriss said on Nov. 19. Cadillac has backed the FIA’s push for a switch to V8 power units from the 2030 F1 season. Earlier this week, the governing body posted graphics saying a new V8 framework had been agreed in principle, then deleted them, leaving the move still unconfirmed. F1 team bosses at the Las Vegas Grand Prix confirmed that there is an agreement in principle, but the FIA has yet to make it official. It wants to put the 2030 rules to the World Motor Sport Council on Dec. 10. Cadillac, the newest team on the grid, has welcomed the move as it gets ready to open its new power unit facility in December. Cadillac Backs FIA for V8 Move “Yeah, I think we’re glad to really see the series coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030, so we’re super happy with that,” Towriss, CEO of Cadillac F1 and TWG Motorsports, said in the FIA press conference in Las Vegas. “Our new power unit facility opens up on December 18th, so as a new manufacturer coming into the sport, the direction is obviously very helpful. We’re excited about the direction, and the crew’s hard at work getting ready.” Asked which engine the new facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, would work on first, Towriss said the team already had a V6 base ready and had started working on V8 designs as well, laying down the foundation to build on. Dan Towriss, CEO of Cadillac F1 and TWG Motorsports, in the FIA press conference at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Nov. 19, 2026. Image Credit: Cadillac F1 Team General Motors Has Worked on Both V6 and V8 Designs “Well, for a period of time, we were working on both,” said Towriss. “So, they’ve already got a V6 base to build off of, and working towards the V8. There are a number of designs that are in motion now, and yeah, so there’s a lot of good foundation for what we’re trying to build and the direction we’re headed in.” Cadillac joined F1 in 2026 as a Ferrari customer team, with General Motors due to supply its own power unit from the 2029 season. Cadillac Will Stay a Ferrari Customer in 2029 Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac MAC-26 and Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari SF-26 at the Dutch Grand Prix, Aug. 21, 2026. Image Credit: Cadillac F1 Team Asked whether it still made sense to build its own engine for 2029, when it would race for only one season before the V8s arrive, Towriss said Cadillac would remain a Ferrari customer through 2029 and start afresh in 2030 as a works team, with General Motors supplying the power unit. “Yeah, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through ’29 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8,” he said.

technology.title: AI could open wallets where ERP upgrade pitches can't, says PwC
technology.description: Global consultancy PwC says IT departments struggling to secure funding for ERP upgrades should make the expected benefits of AI part of their pitch. The Oracle and SAP mega-partner told El Reg that a "clean core" – modern enterprise applications with fewer customizations embedded in the underlying system – makes deploying AI agents easier. Selling that prospect, rather than incremental improvements to existing processes, could help IT leaders justify a migration. Oracle and SAP are both trying to persuade customers to move from established ERP systems to newer platforms. For SAP, that means S/4HANA, preferably in the cloud. For Oracle, it means Fusion Cloud Applications. Moving from ECC or E-Business Suite, respectively, can involve root-and-branch changes to technology and business processes, rather than a straightforward software upgrade. Thousands of organizations still rely on these aging, often heavily customized systems. IT leaders struggle to justify a costly, time-consuming migration when the reward appears to be doing the same meat-and-veg business processes slightly better. For example, a survey of SAP users last year found that 95 percent said building a positive case for migration required substantial effort or was genuinely challenging. Speaking to The Register , Jennifer Colapietro, PwC digital core modernization platform leader, said: "You're seeing it a lot more as part of the rationale for the business case for why they should upgrade, answering the question: 'Why now? What should we prioritize?' Certainly, AI and getting the value of AI, a key business case justification for that. "Folks have budgets for ERP, but now [funding for transformation is] being split because they also have budgets for AI. But there's synergies across them. If you look at moving to a clean digital core ERP, that will help them to realize the AI value faster... be able to turn on AI and be able to start to automate a lot of the processes and implement the agents. That helps to build the business case." SAP recently introduced Joule 2.0 while Oracle has announced Fusion Claw . With both of these new technologies, the vendors are promising customers they can build AI agents to automate business processes and perform some work that was previously done by humans. Colapietro argued that moving to more modern platforms makes deploying AI agents easier and more effective than adding AI capabilities around legacy systems. "It is more challenging to apply AI to the older systems. We focus on the importance of a clean digital core as the foundation for getting the value and effectiveness out of AI and scaling AI responsibly. I think that's given," she said. An ERP replacement isn't the only route to AI, however. European home improvement retailer Kingfisher – which owns the B&Q brand in the UK – eschewed SAP's overtures to upgrade its ECC system, despite encroaching deadlines.
